Q: Python: filtering lists by indices A:

Here is an approach using the package PyFunctional . I learned about this package from the answer What is the Python way of chaining maps and filters? .

from functional import seq

aList = ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'e', 'f', 'g']
myIndices = [0, 3, 4]

vals = seq(myIndices)\
    .map(lambda i: aList[i])\
    .to_list()

print(vals)

The output is ['a', 'd', 'e'].

Q: Powershell script for Searching & uninstalling 7-Zip from all fixed drives A:

It conveniently provides a 'quietuninstallstring'. Note to application developers, putting the version in the install name is not ideal. (powershell 5.1)

# "C:\Program Files\7-Zip\Uninstall.exe" /S
# 7-zip 24.08 (x64)
get-package '7-zip * (x64)' | % { cmd /c $_.metadata['quietuninstallstring'] } }

Q: How would you describe the Java programming language to a beginner? A:

This sounds very familiar to what I went through almost 30 years ago (ouch). I hadn't a clue what the teacher was talking about or how code worked. We were learning Pascal at the time which I would argue is even harder to learn as we were writing DOS programs and had to do memory management. You really needed to understand the computer itself to understand how to write programs for it. With Java less so as the JVM is an abstraction layer.

The main problem was: I didn't like programming. If you don't like something, your brain has a wall around it. No good for learning, no good for understanding. No good for listening either as your attention span goes out the window. That wall needs to come down.

What turned it around for me, in an instant, is that a friend of mine who was also my classmate started to write little games in between classes. And that really flipped the switch for me, being a big gamer. "Wait... I can create my own games!?". That was the moment where I started to religiously learn programming in my off-time (goodbye social life), with the goal of writing my own games and game making tools. I learned C and then C++ before we got a course on it in the next year on my own so I was actually running ahead of the course at that point.

That's the trick... if you want to learn a programming language, you need to be having fun and to have fun you need a goal. Mine was game development, what's yours? Schools, teachers and also employers don't seem to understand that so you have to make it happen on your own. Otherwise I wouldn't have been a software engineer for most of my life now, I am quite sure of that.
